newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Kurd rebels attack oil installation.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Kurd rebels attack oil installation.

text.p: Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas, pursued by Turkish troops in northern Iraq, attacked a small oil installation in southeast Turkey, Anatolian news agency said on Tuesday.

It did not say if there was any damage to the installation in the town of Adiyaman in Monday night's attack. The rebels have stepped up actions inside Turkey in recent days to divert the army's attention from the Iraq operation.
Anatolian said the installation belonged to the state-owned TPAO oil company.
The guerrillas cut the main road from Turkey into Iraq on Sunday night and set fire to two petrol tankers.

Two people were killed and seven injured when two masked gunmen, thought to be PKK rebels, opened fire on a civilian minibus in Turkey's Diyarbakir province on Tuesday morning, local security officials said.

More than 23,000 people have died in 12 years of conflict between troops and the rebels, fighting for Kurdish rule in southeast Turkey. Turkey says it has killed more than 1,000 guerrillas in northern Iraq in the last week.
